solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Benefit of merger, say, shedding a work unit in New York

indicators.note: shedding means dropping, so the word say loses one of its letters

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut

indicators.note: in places the unit of work inside the abbreviation for New York

parts.note: the erg is the CGS unit of work

explanation.surface: A business writer notes a merger's payoff, the trimming of a work unit in a New York office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual 'for example' signal after the definition, but it is fodder; 'shedding' and 'in' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: The extra value two combined companies create beyond their separate worth is the classic boardroom term for what a merger gains.

clue.text: How sad can it be, reshuffling opposition leaders

indicators.note: a reshuffle reorders the letters of these four words, apt for a cabinet change

explanation.surface: A political pundit wonders how bad things could get when a party reshuffles its front bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffling' is both the political term for changing ministers and the signal to rearrange HOWSADCANITBE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British politics, the main opposition party's senior spokespeople, each marking a government minister, form this group.

clue.text: Make short work of English lines collected by star

indicators.note: collected by means held within, so the star word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a nova is a star that flares suddenly in brightness
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL

explanation.surface: An instruction to dash off an English essay quickly, its lines gathered by a star pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make short work of' is an idiom for doing something quickly; only 'short work' defines, 'Make' and 'of' being link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of prose fiction longer than a story but shorter than a full-length book is literally a short work.

clue.text: Quickly make approach

definitions.meaning: to sew up or knock together something in haste, as a dress
the period or sprint leading up to an event, as a bowler's or jumper's

explanation.surface: A terse instruction to make one's approach quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: knocking up clothes fast, and the build-up or preparatory sprint before a jump or bowl.

clue.text: Boyish solver, thoughtful, ought to leave

parts.note: crosswords address the solver as you

indicators.note: to leave means the word ought is removed from the longer word

explanation.surface: A boyish solver who is thoughtful is told he ought to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' is the deletion signal; 'solver' is the crossword convention for the second person.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish looks and energy are those of the young, a straightforward synonym for appearing young.

clue.text: Woman's first man in Middle East

indicators.note: in places the first man inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A woman's first husband was a man from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The French courtesy title for a married lady is used in English for a woman, often one running a brothel.

clue.text: Light cloth mostly covering energy breakfast

indicators.note: covering means the shortened cloth wraps round the energy letter
mostly means the cloth word loses its last letter

parts.note: muslin is a light, loosely woven cotton cloth
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A light cloth is draped over an energy-giving breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSLIN without its last letter is MUSLI; E goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This Swiss mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit is eaten as a morning meal, so it is an example of breakfast.

clue.text: Wimp forgot his lines, hung up on other line

parts.note: a drip is a feeble, wet person
in theatre slang an actor who forgets his lines has dried

explanation.surface: A feeble actor dried on stage and then hung up on another phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' in the definition is a washing line, not an actor's line or a telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes hung on a washing line to drip and dry without wringing are said to be treated this way.

clue.text: Prayer leader regularly immured in cramping zones

indicators.note: cramping means squeezing in, so the zones go between the other letters
regularly means taking every other letter of immured

parts.note: Z is the abbreviation for zone, so two zones give ZZ

explanation.surface: A religious figure is walled up in cramped areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'immured', and 'cramping' squeezes the zones between those and the literal 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who calls Muslims to prayer from a mosque's minaret is a leader of the call to worship.

clue.text: Exciting time, coming by river

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An exciting time is on the way, beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade or thrilling experience is a period of excitement, an apt synonym.

clue.text: Dubliner tempted to incorporate still

indicators.note: to incorporate means the two words contain the run of letters

explanation.surface: An Irishman is tempted to bring something in.
explanation.definitionFit: Motionless or inactive things lie still, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Kindly offered to accept card

indicators.note: to accept means the offering word takes the card inside it

parts.note: tendered means offered, as a resignation
a heart is a playing card of that suit

explanation.surface: Someone kindly offered to take a card.
explanation.definitionFit: A kindly, compassionate person is soft-hearted, a synonym.

clue.text: Swimming pool covers last bit of rear deck

indicators.note: covers means the rearranged pool letters go round the letter from rear
swimming suggests the letters of pool moving about
last bit of means the final letter of rear

explanation.surface: A swimming pool sits under cover at the back of a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' rearranges POOL to OLOP, and R goes inside after the first O.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest deck of a sailing ship, above the hold, is a nautical word for a deck.

clue.text: Six nap fitfully close to futon

parts.note: to half doze is to nap lightly and fitfully

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of futon

explanation.surface: Six people nap restlessly next to a futon.
explanation.definitionFit: Half of twelve is six, so this phrase is a colloquial name for the number.

clue.text: Caught monkey pinching old racket

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the monkey takes the letter inside

parts.note: a langur is an Asian leaf monkey

explanation.surface: A monkey is caught stealing an old tennis racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' is a din, not a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud, clashing, continued noise is a racket, a synonym.

clue.text: Distribute gratuities, ignoring European picker

indicators.note: distribute means the letters of gratuities are handed round into a new order
ignoring means one letter of the fodder is left out of the result

explanation.surface: Someone hands out tips while ignoring a European.
explanation.walkthrough: GRATUITIES with E removed is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plucks the strings of a six-string instrument is said to pick it, so a picker.

clue.text: He's promised work in cafe

indicators.note: work means the letters of in and cafe are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who has made a promise to work in a cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's promised' means he is promised in marriage; 'work' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A man engaged to be married has been promised to his bride, so he is a betrothed man.

clue.text: Stewed ox meat one answer for blood problem

indicators.note: stewed means the letters of ox meat are cooked into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A recipe of stewed ox meat for one, followed by a medical warning.
explanation.walkthrough: OX MEAT rearranges to TOXAEM; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood poisoning by bacterial toxins is a medical condition affecting the blood.

clue.text: Flat piece journalist's brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the journalist's letters go inside the piece

parts.note: a bit is a piece
ED is the abbreviation for editor, a journalist; with 's gives EDS

explanation.surface: A journalist's article is published as a flat piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room rented flat with bed and living space combined is a British kind of flat.

clue.text: Abandons son leaving courses

indicators.note: leaving means the son letter goes out of the courses word

parts.note: desserts are courses of a meal

explanation.surface: A son walks out of meal courses, abandoning the family.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away from and leave someone in the lurch is a synonym of abandoning them.

clue.text: Good getting on high-priority film

parts.note: getting on means growing old
a rush job is one given high priority

explanation.surface: A good, ageing director has an urgent film project.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin's 1925 silent comedy set in the Klondike is a famous film with this title.

clue.text: Blue Berets stayed guarding male in a mess

parts.note: UN peacekeepers wear blue berets

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding, so the stayed word holds the male letter

parts.note: kept means stayed, as in kept calm

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers stayed to guard a man in a mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' is untidiness, not the soldiers' dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy, dishevelled hair or appearance is uncombed, describing someone in a mess.

clue.text: A billionaire's gems

parts.note: Bill Gates is a billionaire; the 's is read as is, linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A billionaire's precious stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Banded chalcedony stones are semi-precious gems, an example of the class.

clue.text: Lost again at sea, longing for home

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of lost again are muddled

explanation.surface: A sailor lost again at sea longs for home.
explanation.definitionFit: A wistful yearning for the past or for one's homeland is homesickness, the word's original sense.

clue.text: Excellent posh weekends during every year

indicators.note: during means inside, so the letters go within the yearly abbreviation

parts.note: PA is per annum, every year
U means upper-class, posh
the end of the word week is K, so two weekends give KK

explanation.surface: Posh weekends every year are judged excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weekends' is read as the end letters of 'week' twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindi-derived Anglo-Indian word for genuine or first-class, used in posh British slang for excellent.

clue.text: Icy rivers protect city

indicators.note: protect means the rivers stand around the city

parts.note: the Po is an Italian river and R is the abbreviation for river
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Frozen rivers protect a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The regions round the earth's poles are frozen, so this adjective means extremely cold.

clue.text: Mariners start to inscribe bone collections

parts.note: tars are sailors

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of inscribe

explanation.surface: Sailors begin to carve their collections of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the ankle's group of bones, each such group being a collection of small bones.

clue.text: Magazine writer's breaking reading deadline

parts.note: Time is a news magazine

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the writer's letters go inside the reading word

parts.note: lit, short for literature, is reading matter
the writer's is I am, contracted to IM

explanation.surface: A magazine writer is breaking off his reading for a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's' is the setter saying 'I am', IM.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-off point by which a task must be completed is a fixed temporal limit, a synonym.

clue.text: A sibling maintains pose unchanged

indicators.note: maintains means holds within, so the sibling word keeps the pose word inside

parts.note: sis is short for sister
SETTER'S SLIP: pose naturally gives SIT, which makes one S too many; only IT fits, and the setter apologised for the error

explanation.surface: A sister keeps her pose without changing.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue is faulty, as the setter Redshank admitted on the blog: 'pose' gives SIT, and A SIS 'maintains' SIT gives ASSITIS, one S too many. Only IT inside SIS gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning in the present state, without alteration, as when goods are sold without changes.

clue.text: Beer with no heart judged to have a head?

definitions.note: a past participle phrase: treated with gas so as to froth on top

indicators.note: with no heart means the middle letter of the beer word is removed

parts.note: ale is beer
rated means judged

explanation.surface: A judge decides a heartless beer ought to have a head.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: gassed beer has a frothy head.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging a liquid with gas makes it bubbly, which gives a beer its foaming top.
